sources.entry: UUSEC WAF - Industry-leading high-performance, AI and semantic technology web application firewall and API security gateway (fork of nginx). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C/Lua/Docker

summary.one_liner: UUSEC WAF is a free, nginx-based web application firewall and API security gateway that uses machine learning and semantic analysis engines to block web attacks.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a reverse-proxy WAF built on nginx and LuaJIT, deployed via Docker and Docker Compose and managed through a web admin backend. It claims an anomaly-detection approach that learns normal parameter patterns to build whitelist rules, aiming to block zero-day attacks without new rules. It includes four semantic detection engines (SQL, XSS, RCE, LFI) and decoding of base64, JSON and form data. It supports traditional rule creation plus Lua script rules and plugins, with rules taking effect without restarting. The README also mentions a cache purge feature using regex URL matching, and host-level (HIPS) and runtime (RASP, for Java JVM and PHP Zend) protection. Responses carry a server header of uuWAF, and HTTPS certificates can be uploaded or obtained via Let's Encrypt.
use_cases: protect a website from SQL injection and XSS attacks
reverse-proxy WAF in front of existing web servers
API security gateway for web traffic
block zero-day web vulnerabilities without rule updates
manage HTTPS certificates and Let's Encrypt renewal for protected sites
CDN-style caching with regex-based cache purge
how_to_run: Install Docker CE 20.10.14 or above and Docker Compose 2.0.0 or above
Run the installer: sudo bash -c "$(curl -fsSL ...)" (URL truncated in README)
Log in to the management UI with the default username admin and password #Passw0rd (change it)
Add a site domain and its backend server IP under the Sites menu
Upload an SSL certificate or request a Let's Encrypt certificate, then point the domain's DNS A record to the WAF server
notable: Semantic analysis engines for SQL, XSS, RCE and LFI instead of only regex rules
Machine-learning whitelist generation from normal traffic parameters
Lua script rules and plugin extension
RASP instrumentation for Java JVM and PHP Zend runtimes
Regex-based URL cache purge beyond commercial nginx proxy_cache_purge wildcard matching
caveats: README recommends a pure Linux x86_64 server because it needs ports 80 and 443 by default
Requires Docker CE and Docker Compose with specific minimum versions
Effect comparison table is labeled 'for reference only' and is vendor-provided; the Pro edition results are from the vendor
Some features (Pro edition, full documentation) are referenced via an official website not included in the README
